preamble: Fronting of the voiced retroflex fricative [ʐ] to the voiced alveolar fricative [z]. In Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland, parts of Silesia) the retroflex sibilant series /ʂ, ʐ, t͡ʂ, d͡ʐ/ merged with the dental series, so ż [ʐ] is pronounced [z]; ż from the old trill rz is excluded, since rz developed separately and stays [ʐ] (przed [pʂɛt] in both dialect types). The change is attested only in this Polish dialect area and in a few Belarusian villages that borrowed it from Polish.

examples.note: Mazurating dialects merge the postalveolar/retroflex sibilants with the dentals.
Both ż [ʐ] and dż are fronted in the same word.

sources: Gogolewski, S. (2001). Dialectology in Poland, 1873-1997. In Koerner, E. F. K. & Szwedek, A. (eds.), Towards a History of Linguistics in Poland. John Benjamins. https://books.google.com/books?id=CTtT7-JTwioC&pg=PA128
